- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate during low sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — model is overly conservative, misses upward momentum.
- Lag in response to recent price spikes — model often delays reaction, especially if sentiment is rising.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to premature declines after peaks.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment swings, not long-term trend — ignore short-term sentiment noise.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid shifts), model overfits to recent sentiment, leading to erratic forecasts — smooth sentiment transitions before forecasting.
- Avoid forecasting upward if sentiment is declining after a spike — model often ignores sentiment reversal signals.
